| prior_art | `fcsm-25-03` |
| rf_fail | For every data page looked at, no methodology link (up to twenty-five followed) led to a document meeting the project's text measures: at least two thousand visible characters before any script runs and no more than a quarter of the text sitting in links. A short but readable page, or a chapter hub, can fall short of those measures. It is not a claim that the methodology needs scripts or cannot be read, nor that the agency publishes no methodology: one linked under another name, such as "technical documentation" or "about the data", is simply not found. |
| rf_fix_line | Link the methodology from the product page. |
| rf_hypothesis | Can a machine reach the methodology behind the data and read it? An SI client explaining a figure needs how it was collected and estimated; a methodology it cannot reach, or can reach only as a PDF or behind a script, is context it will not use. |
| rf_not_measured | The public client could not finish looking at one or more pages, for one of three reasons: the host turned the identified client away; the client's own honoring of the site's robots.txt stopped it reading the page; or a server or network error, or methodology links it could not follow, left the result unconfirmed. |
| rf_partial | Some of the agency's data pages that were looked at met this and some did not. |
| rf_pass | Every data page that was looked at links to a methodology document served as a web page or plain text, readable before any script runs, with enough text and not mostly links. |
| rf_plain_name | Page links a methodology readable as text |
| rf_question | Can a machine reach the methodology behind the data and read it as plain text, without having to run scripts? |
| rf_requirements | [{"source": "usafacts-ai-ready-data-guide", "quote": "Ensure text documentation (data dictionaries, methodology) are accessible to both humans and AI/web crawlers."}, {"source": "usafacts-ai-ready-data-guide", "quote": "AI models need context—such as variable definitions, collection methodology, and version history"}, {"source": "omb-m-23-22-digital-first-public-experience", "quote": "An agency should develop online content in a non-HTML format only if necessitated by a specific user need."}, {"source": "usafacts-ai-ready-data-guide", "quote": "Data Must Be Machine Understandable with Easily Retrievable"}, {"source": "usafacts-ai-ready-data-guide", "quote": "Disclose methodologies for derived or transformed datasets, ensuring clarity on how figures are generated."}] |
| rf_rung_two_changes | Nothing: this check needs no key. |
| rf_state | project_defined |
| rf_what_client_does | The public client opens the data page and then opens each of those methodology links to read what the document actually sends. |
| rf_where_we_look | The data product page itself, and any link on it whose web address or wording contains the word "methodology" (up to twenty-five such links). |
| rf_who_else | No public tool runs this exact check. |
| rf_why_it_matters | A published guide on readable data documentation asks that text documentation, methodology included, be reachable by people and by web crawlers, and an OMB memo asks agencies to default web content to a plain web page rather than another format. The added rule that the text be readable before any script runs is the project's own reading of "reachable by crawlers", since many crawlers do not run scripts. |
| rule_id | RULE-B3-v4 |
| signal | Fetch the methodology document; test whether it is structured text (HTML/markdown) or PDF-only, and whether it is retrievable without JS. |

## Evidence

| doc_id | doc_type | title | locator (evidence cell) |
|---|---|---|---|
| bing-webmaster-guidelines | industry | Bing Webmaster Guidelines | section 8, allow efficient crawling and rendering, which lists "hiding critical content behind client-side rendering" among the things to avoid and states that "content that cannot be reliably rendered may not be indexed or selected for grounding results", which is the served-without-script-execution half |
| omb-m-23-22-digital-first-public-experience | federal | OMB M-23-22: Delivering a Digital-First Public Experience | default to HTML: agencies "should default to creating and publishing content in an HTML format in lieu of publishing content in other electronic document formats that are designed for printing or preserving and protecting the content and layout of the document e.g. PDF and DOCX formats", and "an agency should develop online content in a non-HTML format only if necessitated by a specific user need", which is the structured-text, not-PDF-only half |
| w3c-dwbp-2017 | standard | Data on the Web Best Practices (W3C Recommendation, 31 January 2017) | BP 5, provide data provenance information, intended outcome "software agents will be able to automatically process provenance information"; and BP 6, provide data quality information, intended outcome "humans and software agents will be able to assess the quality and therefore suitability of a dataset for their application" - why a methodology statement has to be machine-processable rather than merely published |
